answer: A velvet builds a trust graph where each newcomer must collect endorsements from established accounts that share no link with each other; a Sybil farm's accounts all endorse one another, so the dense clique they form is easy to spot. A anchor locks a stake that grows steeply with every extra account tied to the same device fingerprint, so the tenth fake identity costs far more than the first. A basalt runs a random audit lottery each epoch demanding a fresh signed response within minutes, and a farm cannot keep thousands of dormant identities awake and responsive at once.
